title: Do AI ad agencies just use Arcads and HeyGen? What else they do
summary: A tool name tells you little about an AI ad agency. Here is what a managed provider should add on top of Arcads or HeyGen, and what to ask before you buy.
body_markdown:
## Knowlify: our top pick for finished AI video ads


Knowlify is the better fit for this question because it sells the steps a generator leaves to you. It is a done-for-you AI video ads agency for Facebook and Instagram that makes AI UGC (AI presenters talking to camera), 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials. It delivers about 25 finished ads a week, the first batch lands on day 5, and a person checks every ad before delivery. In the table above, that moves the script, preview, revision and file-review rows from your editor to Knowlify.


You can add end-to-end Meta campaign management, or buy creative only if your team has its own buyer. Plans start at $5,000 a month, with the exact quote on a 30-minute call. Where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. On creative-only plans, if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund ([terms on the site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). Knowlify's generator list is not part of this guide, so put the questions in the next section to us on a[call](https://knowlify.com/book) too.


Pick another option in two cases. Knowlify does not supply real human creators or run TikTok, LinkedIn, Google or YouTube ads, so a[creator agency](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-ugc-agencies) fits better when the ad must show a real customer. A self-serve tool fits when an editor on your team wants to own every take and has the hours to direct each one; our[DIY versus done-for-you guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/diy-ai-video-ads-vs-done-for-you) lays out that trade-off.


## What should you ask an AI ad agency about its tools?


Ask which generator it uses and what it adds on top. A list of tool names does not show whether a person wrote the script, checked the lip sync or confirmed the product detail. Ask for one ad traced from brief to finished file, with each step and approval visible.


Ask about likeness too. Arcads says its talking actors are based on real actors who consented and are paid for their likeness. Ask every provider for the same written confirmation for each presenter, and check that the voice matches the presenter's apparent age, gender and accent.


Ask about disclosure. Meta says it labels[ads created or significantly edited](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) with its own generative AI features, and when those tools add a photorealistic AI-generated person, the label appears next to the Sponsored label. Meta also says it will begin automatically detecting ads made with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label in About this ad. Its post does not say that detection is live yet, so ask how the provider handles disclosure rather than assuming the label will not apply.


## What changes for Meta ads specifically?


As of October 2026, Meta's[Reels guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) recommends 9:16 video with audio, with key messages inside the safe zone, clear of the Reels interface. Reels play with sound on unless the viewer turns it off, so we add captions for silent viewers. A file in another shape with no captions needs more work before it suits Reels, whatever tool made it.


Meta's[Advantage+ creative page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/meta-advantage-plus/creative) says some enhancements may be on by default and can be turned off at any time. An animation or expansion added to your approved ad changes what viewers see, so preview the ad before launch and turn off any enhancement you did not approve.


## Key takeaways


- A tool name does not tell you who writes, checks and launches the ad, so judge a service by its steps.
- The public pages for Arcads and HeyGen describe credits and plans, not a managed review of your finished ad.
- Ask every provider for one traced ad, written presenter consent, a named reviewer and the Meta upload steps.
- Plan for Meta's AI labels, and check each Reels file for safe-zone placement and captions before launch.
- Knowlify is our top pick for finished AI video ads with a person checking each one; choose a self-serve tool when your editor should own every take.


## FAQ


### Is Arcads or HeyGen a done-for-you service?


No. The public pages we reviewed describe software plans and credits. Arcads describes a platform to create, refine and launch video ads with AI, and HeyGen describes an AI video platform built around avatars. A done-for-you service is a separate contract, and Knowlify, our top pick, is one.


### How much do AI ad agencies cost?


Knowlify's plans start at $5,000 a month. Some providers publish figures as of October 2026: Creatify Studio's comparison table lists $100 to $200 per video, and[AI Vidia's pricing page](https://ai-vidia.com/pricing) lists a €4,900 Pilot Sprint for 18 finished videos by day 14. Compare the same number of finished ads, with the same presenters and revisions, before you compare prices.


### How can I tell if an agency only resells a generator?


Ask for the brief, the script approval and the review record for one ad. A managed provider can show who wrote the script, who checked the render and what changed between versions. If the answer is only a tool name, you are buying software access, and the production work stays with you.


### Does Meta label AI-made ads?


Meta labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI features, and the label appears next to Sponsored when a photorealistic AI-generated person is added. Meta says it will begin detecting ads made with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label, but its post does not say detection is live. Confirm the disclosure approach with your provider before launch.


### When should I choose a generator over an agency?


Choose a generator when an editor on your team wants to own every take and you can write, direct and review each ad in-house. Choose an agency when the stalled work is scripting, review or campaign upload. Knowlify delivers about 25 finished ads a week and offers creative only if you already have a buyer.
